[edit]

In South Korea, "Ditto" topped the Circle Digital Chart for a record-breaking 13 weeks, longer than any other song in the chart history. It peaked at number eight on the *Billboard* Global 200; topped the charts in Indonesia, Singapore, Taiwan, and Vietnam; and reached the top 10 in Japan, Hong Kong, Malaysia, and the Philippines. Both the Korea Music Content Association (KMCA) and the Recording Industry Association of Japan (RIAJ) certified "Ditto" platinum for surpassing 100 million streams in respective countries.




## Background and release

[edit]

South Korean girl group NewJeans released their first eponymous extended play (EP) in August 2022 to commercial success and critical acclaim. The EP topped South Korea's Circle Music Chart,[1] selling 311,200 copies in its first week.[2]

US, peaking at number four with 41.9 million streams and 3,000 digital downloads sold in the period of December 30, 2022–January 5, 2023.[61] It debuted at number 36 on the *Billboard* Global 200 in the chart issue dated December 31, 2022,[62] and peaked at number eight two weeks later with 46.5 million streams and 4,000 digital downloads sold, making NewJeans the fourth Korean group to enter the chart's top-10 after BTS, Blackpink, and Big Bang.[63]

<title>Get Up (EP)</title>
<fragment>
The EP's first single, "Super Shy", was released for digital download and streaming on July 7, 2023, along with the B-side track "New Jeans".[2] It was promoted in partnership with YouTube Shorts through a dance challenge released under the hashtag "ImSuperShy".[30] In South Korea, "Super Shy" topped the Circle Digital Chart, earning NewJeans their third number-one single in the country.[31] Internationally, "Super Shy" became the group's best-performing track on numerous charts, including the US *Billboard* Hot 100 and the UK Singles Chart, and reached number one in Hong Kong, Malaysia, Singapore, and Taiwan.[32][33] "Cool with You" and "ETA" were released as the next singles along with the EP on July 21, 2023.

## **NewJeans - "Super Shy"、"Cool With You"、"ETA"**

这些歌曲都来自NewJeans的第二张EP《Get Up》（2023年7月21日发行），该专辑取得了巨大的商业成功：

这首歌来自BOYNEXTDOOR的首张单曲专辑《Who!》（2023年5月30日发行）：

- 韩国销量：246,443张

- **playlist覆盖**: 知名艺人更容易进入重要歌单

- 随着粉丝基础扩大，数字表现有望提升

- 全球化背景下，英语歌曲天然优势明显
- K-pop国际化程度决定数字表现上限
- 流媒体已经成为新的"销量标准"

这些数据反映出当前音乐产业的真实竞争格局，也预示着未来可能的发展方向。

File:Dua Lipa 2019.jpg"Levitating" by Dua Lipa *(pictured)* became the first number one single of a Global 200 year-end list. It achieved this despite peaking at number two on the weekly Global 200 chart.[1]
The *Billboard* Global 200 and Global Excl. US are charts that ranks the best-performing singles globally and globally excluding the United States, respectively. Its data is published by *Billboard* weekly and based collectively on each single's weekly physical and digital sales, as well as streaming. At the end of a year, *Billboard* publishes an annual list of the 200 most successful songs throughout that year on the Global 200 and Global Excl. US charts based on the information. For 2021, its first year, the list was published on December 2, calculated with data from November 21, 2020, to November 13, 2021.

In August 2018, *Billboard* published a new edition of the "Greatest of All Time Hot 100 Singles" chart, its list of the 100 best-performing songs in the history of the Hot 100. "Shape of You" was ranked at number nine, the third-highest position of any song released in the 2010s (behind only "Uptown Funk" by Mark Ronson featuring Bruno Mars and "Party Rock Anthem" by LMFAO featuring Lauren Bennett and GoonRock).[70]


On November 23, 2021, *Billboard* published an updated edition of the "Greatest of All Time Hot 100 Singles" chart from 2018 where "Shape of You" is currently ranked the #10 Greatest Hot 100 Hit of All Time following the induction of the Weeknd's 2019 single "Blinding Lights" which currently holds the #1 position.[71]

**Record sales** or **music sales** are activities related to selling music recordings (albums, singles, or music videos) through physical record shops or digital music stores.[1][2][3] Record sales reached their peak in 1999, when 600 million people spent an average of $64 on records, achieving $40 billion in sales of recorded music.[4][5] Sales continued declining in the 21st century.[6][7] The collapse of record sales also made artists rely on touring for most of their income.[8] By 2019, record sales accounted for less than half of global recorded music revenue, overtaken by streaming.[9] Following the inclusion of streaming into record charts in the mid-2010s, record sales are also referred to as **traditional sales** or **pure sales**.[10][11][12]

Based on my research, I can provide detailed information about how record sales are categorized and how the industry has evolved.

## **Categorization of Record Sales**

The recording industry categorizes sales into three main types:

### **1. Physical Sales**
- **Formats**: Vinyl records, CDs, cassette tapes, DVDs
- **Traditional metric**: Pure sales (actual physical units sold)
- **Historical dominance**: This was the primary metric from the invention of the phonograph (1877) until the digital era
- **Peak impact**: Physical sales reached their peak in 1999 when the industry generated $40 billion in revenue

### **2. Digital Sales** 
- **Formats**: Digital downloads, digital albums, ringtones
- **Emergence**: Became significant in the 2000s as iTunes and other digital stores grew
- **Certification inclusion**: Many certifying bodies (like RIAA) now include digital sales in their traditional sales figures
- **Decline**: Digital downloads have been declining since the rise of streaming

### **3. Streaming Sales**
- **Modern metric**: Streams are converted to "album-equivalent units"
- **Inclusion in charts**: Streaming was incorporated into record charts in the mid-2010s
- **Revenue dominance**: By 2019, streaming overtook traditional sales as the primary revenue source for recorded music

## **Certification Bodies and Their Approach**

**Key Examples from Global Certifying Bodies:**

- **United States (RIAA)**: 
  - Gold: 500,000 units, Platinum: 1,000,000 units, Diamond: 10,000,000 units
  - Now includes both physical and digital sales in traditional certifications

- **Germany**: 
  - Modern singles (since 2003): Gold: 200,000, Platinum: 400,000
  - Pre-2003 singles had different thresholds
  - Jazz singles have special lower thresholds

- **International Recognition**: Countries like Australia, UK, Canada, and many European nations now include digital sales in their physical certification figures

## **Industry Impact on Record-Settling**

This evolution creates significant challenges for comparing historical best-selling records:

### **The "White Christmas" vs "Candle in the Wind 1997" Case**

- **Bing Crosby's "White Christmas" (1942)**: Estimated 50+ million copies sold worldwide
  - ✅ **All-time best-selling single** (Guinness recognizes this)
  - ⚠️ **Pre-chart era**: Released before modern charting began
  - 📊 **Sales primarily physical**: Limited digital potential

- **Elton John's "Candle in the Wind 1997"**: Approximately 33 million copies sold
  - ✅ **Best single since charts began** (Guinness 2009)
  - 📈 **Peak era release**: Benefited from global distribution systems
  - 🎤 **Physical sales dominated**: Released before streaming became significant

### **Modern Era Implications**

- **Streaming dilution**: Today's hits need billions of streams to match physical sales figures
- **Chart evolution**: Artists can now have "number one" hits primarily through streaming
- **Revenue shift**: By 2019, traditional sales accounted for less than half of global recorded music revenue

## **The "All-Time" Record Approach**

The industry essentially uses a **two-tier approach**:

1. **True all-time records**: Include pre-chart era hits where sales are estimated
2. **Modern era records**: Measure post-chart era sales more precisely but exclude massive historical sellers

This creates the situation where both "White Christmas" and more modern hits can claim different versions of "best-selling" based on measurement parameters.

The evolution from pure physical sales → digital sales → streaming equivalents reflects both technological advancement and changing business models in the music industry, making direct historical comparisons increasingly complex.

In August 2018, *Billboard* published a new edition of the "Greatest of All Time Hot 100 Singles" chart, its list of the 100 best-performing songs in the history of the Hot 100. On November 23, 2021, *Billboard* published an updated edition of the "Greatest of All Time Hot 100 Singles" chart from 2018 where "Shape of You" is currently ranked the #10 Greatest Hot 100 Hit of All Time following the induction of the Weeknd's 2019 single "Blinding Lights" which currently holds the #1 position.[71]

<document>
<title>Digital Song Sales</title>
<fragment>
This article is about the Billboard music chart. For digital music, see Music download.





![](image)Billboard logo (From 2013)
The **Digital Songs** or **Digital Song Sales** chart (previously named **Hot Digital Songs**)[1] ranks the best-selling digital songs in the United States, as compiled by Nielsen SoundScan and published by *Billboard* magazine. Although it originally started tracking song sales the week of October 30, 2004,[2] it officially debuted in the issue dated January 22, 2005, and merged all versions of a song sold from digital music distributors.[3] Its data was incorporated in the Hot 100 three weeks later. Since October 2004, digital sales have been incorporated into many of *Billboard*'s music singles charts.[4] The decision was based on the dramatic increase of the digital market while commercial single sales in a physical format were becoming negligible.[5]


The first number one song on the Digital Songs chart was "Just Lose It" by Eminem.[2]

<document>
<title>International Federation of the Phonographic Industry</title>
<fragment>

Launched in January 2014,[24] the IFPI Global Recording Artist Chart (sometimes called just the IFPI Global Artist Chart) was the first global chart to accurately capture the popularity of artists across streaming channels, alongside digital and physical album and singles sales. The independently verified[33] chart includes sales of albums across digital, CD and vinyl formats; singles, both downloaded and physical; and streams across the calendar year. The chart includes all the music of each artist featured, not just one track or album. It uses album equivalent units to combine measurements of downloads, physical sales and streams.


</fragment>
<fragment>

IFPI also publishes a list of the top 10 best-performing global singles and albums each year. The most recent winners, for 2022, were Harry Styles' 'As It Was'[42] and Bad Bunny's 'Un Verano Sin Ti'[43] respectively. In March 2022 IFPI launched the first ever Global Vinyl Album Chart (most recently topped by Taylor Swift's 'Midnights', announced in March 2023) and in March 2023 they introduced the IFPI Global Streaming Album Chart, with Bad Bunny's 'Un Verano Sin Ti' taking the top spot. The most recently announced IFPI Global Album Sales Chart saw Jay Chou's 'Greatest Works of Art' at no. 1[44] – the first Asian artist to top an IFPI Global Chart.


</fragment>
</document>

The *Billboard* Hot 100 is a chart that ranks the best-performing singles of the United States. Its data, published by *Billboard* magazine and compiled by Nielsen SoundScan, is based collectively on each single's weekly physical and digital sales, as well as airplay and streaming. At the end of a year, *Billboard* will publish an annual list of the 100 most successful songs throughout that year on the Hot 100 chart based on the information. For 2015, the list was published on December 9, calculated with data from December 6, 2014, to November 28, 2015.[1]

<fragment>
![](image)"Uptown Funk" by Mark Ronson featuring Bruno Mars came in at number one, spending a total of fourteen consecutive weeks at the top position of the *Billboard* Hot 100 during 2015.
The *Billboard* Hot 100 is a chart that ranks the best-performing singles of the United States. Its data, published by *Billboard* magazine and compiled by Nielsen SoundScan, is based collectively on each single's weekly physical and digital sales, as well as airplay and streaming. At the end of a year, *Billboard* will publish an annual list of the 100 most successful songs throughout that year on the Hot 100 chart based on the information. For 2015, the list was published on December 9, calculated with data from December 6, 2014, to November 28, 2015.[1]

</fragment>
<fragment>
The funk track "Uptown Funk" by British producer Mark Ronson, featuring American singer Bruno Mars, who co-wrote and voiced the lyrics was named the number 1 song of 2015, despite being released in late 2014. It spent the longest time at number 1 for the year, 14 weeks, and spent the entire year in the Top 40 region. This is also the joint-fifth longest time at number 1 for a single in the history of the Hot 100 post-1958 inception, after Lil Nas X and Billy Ray Cyrus's "Old Town Road" (19 weeks), Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men's "One Sweet Day" and Luis Fonsi, Daddy Yankee and Justin Bieber's "Despacito" (16 weeks), and Harry Styles' "As It Was" (15 weeks).

<title>Billboard Year-End</title>
<fragment>

After *Billboard* began obtaining sales and airplay information from Nielsen SoundScan and Nielsen Broadcast Data Systems, the year-end charts are now calculated by a very straightforward cumulative total of yearlong sales (or sales and airplay) points.[*citation needed*] This gives a more accurate picture of any given year's most popular titles, as an entry that hypothetically spent nine weeks at number one in the spring could possibly have earned fewer cumulative points than one spending six weeks at number three in January.


</fragment>

<document>
<title>Digital Song Sales</title>
<fragment>
This article is about the Billboard music chart. For digital music, see Music download.





![](image)Billboard logo (From 2013)
The **Digital Songs** or **Digital Song Sales** chart (previously named **Hot Digital Songs**)[1] ranks the best-selling digital songs in the United States, as compiled by Nielsen SoundScan and published by *Billboard* magazine. Although it originally started tracking song sales the week of October 30, 2004,[2] it officially debuted in the issue dated January 22, 2005, and merged all versions of a song sold from digital music distributors.[3] Its data was incorporated in the Hot 100 three weeks later. Since October 2004, digital sales have been incorporated into many of *Billboard*'s music singles charts.[4] The decision was based on the dramatic increase of the digital market while commercial single sales in a physical format were becoming negligible.[5]


The first number one song on the Digital Songs chart was "Just Lose It" by Eminem.[2]


</fragment>
</document>

<document>
<title>Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2016</title>
<fragment>
The *Billboard* Hot 100 is a chart that ranks the best-performing singles of the United States. Its data, published by *Billboard* magazine and compiled by Nielsen SoundScan, is based collectively on each single's weekly physical and digital sales, as well as airplay and streaming. At the end of a year, *Billboard* will publish an annual list of the 100 most successful songs throughout that year on the Hot 100 chart based on the information. For 2016, the list was published on December 8, calculated with data from December 5, 2015 to November 26, 2016. The 2016 list was dominated by Justin Bieber and Drake, who shared the top four spots, marking the first time two artists took up the top four spots since 2009 with Lady Gaga and The Black Eyed Peas.[1]


</fragment>

<title>Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2016</title>
<fragment>
The *Billboard* Hot 100 is a chart that ranks the best-performing singles of the United States. <document>
<title>Digital Song Sales</title>
<fragment>
This article is about the Billboard music chart. For digital music, see Music download.





![](image)Billboard logo (From 2013)
The **Digital Songs** or **Digital Song Sales** chart (previously named **Hot Digital Songs**)[1] ranks the best-selling digital songs in the United States, as compiled by Nielsen SoundScan and published by *Billboard* magazine. Although it originally started tracking song sales the week of October 30, 2004,[2] it officially debuted in the issue dated January 22, 2005, and merged all versions of a song sold from digital music distributors.[3] Its data was incorporated in the Hot 100 three weeks later. Since October 2004, digital sales have been incorporated into many of *Billboard*'s music singles charts.[4] The decision was based on the dramatic increase of the digital market while commercial single sales in a physical format were becoming negligible.[5]


The first number one song on the Digital Songs chart was "Just Lose It" by Eminem.[2]

**1. Ed Sheeran - "Shape of You"**

Taylor Swift had an excellent year in the **Billboard Digital Song Sales** chart in 2017:

- **Most number-one singles**: She reached #1 on the Digital Song Sales chart with **five different songs** - the most by any artist that year
- **Songs that hit #1**: "I Don't Wanna Live Forever" (with Zayn), "Look What You Made Me Do", "...Ready for It?", "Gorgeous", and "Call It What You Want"

- **Year-end ranking**: While one of her songs ("I Don't Wanna Live Forever") made Billboard's Year-End Hot 100 at #26, none reached the top tier in terms of overall global digital sales that year

It's worth noting that while Taylor Swift dominated the weekly Digital Song Sales chart in America, the global top sellers like Ed Sheeran and Luis Fonsi achieved higher overall worldwide sales numbers for their massive hits.

<title>Digital Song Sales</title>
<fragment>
This article is about the Billboard music chart. For digital music, see Music download.





![](image)Billboard logo (From 2013)
The **Digital Songs** or **Digital Song Sales** chart (previously named **Hot Digital Songs**)[1] ranks the best-selling digital songs in the United States, as compiled by Nielsen SoundScan and published by *Billboard* magazine. Although it originally started tracking song sales the week of October 30, 2004,[2] it officially debuted in the issue dated January 22, 2005, and merged all versions of a song sold from digital music distributors.[3] Its data was incorporated in the Hot 100 three weeks later. Since October 2004, digital sales have been incorporated into many of *Billboard*'s music singles charts.[4] The decision was based on the dramatic increase of the digital market while commercial single sales in a physical format were becoming negligible.[5]


The first number one song on the Digital Songs chart was "Just Lose It" by Eminem.[2]

<title>Digital Song Sales</title>
<fragment>
This article is about the Billboard music chart. For digital music, see Music download.





![](image)Billboard logo (From 2013)
The **Digital Songs** or **Digital Song Sales** chart (previously named **Hot Digital Songs**)[1] ranks the best-selling digital songs in the United States, as compiled by Nielsen SoundScan and published by *Billboard* magazine. Although it originally started tracking song sales the week of October 30, 2004,[2] it officially debuted in the issue dated January 22, 2005, and merged all versions of a song sold from digital music distributors.[3] Its data was incorporated in the Hot 100 three weeks later. Since October 2004, digital sales have been incorporated into many of *Billboard*'s music singles charts.[4] The decision was based on the dramatic increase of the digital market while commercial single sales in a physical format were becoming negligible.[5]


The first number one song on the Digital Songs chart was "Just Lose It" by Eminem.[2]

<title>Digital Song Sales</title>
<fragment>
This article is about the Billboard music chart. For digital music, see Music download.





![](image)Billboard logo (From 2013)
The **Digital Songs** or **Digital Song Sales** chart (previously named **Hot Digital Songs**)[1] ranks the best-selling digital songs in the United States, as compiled by Nielsen SoundScan and published by *Billboard* magazine. Although it originally started tracking song sales the week of October 30, 2004,[2] it officially debuted in the issue dated January 22, 2005, and merged all versions of a song sold from digital music distributors.[3] Its data was incorporated in the Hot 100 three weeks later. Since October 2004, digital sales have been incorporated into many of *Billboard*'s music singles charts.[4] The decision was based on the dramatic increase of the digital market while commercial single sales in a physical format were becoming negligible.[5]


The first number one song on the Digital Songs chart was "Just Lose It" by Eminem.[2]

The data are compiled by Nielsen SoundScan based on each single's weekly digital sales, which combines sales of different versions of a song by an act for a summarized figure.

![](image)Rapper Lil Nas X, *(pictured)* earned his first digital song number one with "Old Town Road". The song has spent sixteen non-consecutive weeks at number one.

<document>
<title>Digital Song Sales</title>
<fragment>
This article is about the Billboard music chart. For digital music, see Music download.





![](image)Billboard logo (From 2013)
The **Digital Songs** or **Digital Song Sales** chart (previously named **Hot Digital Songs**)[1] ranks the best-selling digital songs in the United States, as compiled by Nielsen SoundScan and published by *Billboard* magazine. Although it originally started tracking song sales the week of October 30, 2004,[2] it officially debuted in the issue dated January 22, 2005, and merged all versions of a song sold from digital music distributors.[3] Its data was incorporated in the Hot 100 three weeks later. Since October 2004, digital sales have been incorporated into many of *Billboard*'s music singles charts.[4] The decision was based on the dramatic increase of the digital market while commercial single sales in a physical format were becoming negligible.[5]


The first number one song on the Digital Songs chart was "Just Lose It" by Eminem.[2]


</fragment>
<fragment>
* "Rolling in the Deep" by Adele holds the record for the most digitally downloaded song in a calendar year.[24]
* "Payphone" by Maroon 5 featuring Wiz Khalifa holds the record for the largest debut/overall sales week for a group for a digital song with 493,000 downloads.[25]
* "We Are Young" by Fun. featuring Janelle Monáe is the first song to log seven weeks of 300,000 or more in digital sales.[26]
* "Thrift Shop" by Macklemore and Ryan Lewis featuring Wanz is the first song to log eight and nine weeks of 300,000 or more in digital sales.[27]
* "Blurred Lines" by Robin Thicke featuring T.I. and Pharrell is the first song to log 10 weeks of 300,000 or more in digital sales and the first song to log four weeks of 400,000 or more in digital sales.
* "Somebody That I Used to Know" by Gotye featuring Kimbra is the first song to log three weeks of 400,000 or more in digital sales.

This article is about the Billboard music chart. For digital music, see Music download.





![](image)Billboard logo (From 2013)
The **Digital Songs** or **Digital Song Sales** chart (previously named **Hot Digital Songs**)[1] ranks the best-selling digital songs in the United States, as compiled by Nielsen SoundScan and published by *Billboard* magazine. Although it originally started tracking song sales the week of October 30, 2004,[2] it officially debuted in the issue dated January 22, 2005, and merged all versions of a song sold from digital music distributors.[3] Its data was incorporated in the Hot 100 three weeks later. Since October 2004, digital sales have been incorporated into many of *Billboard*'s music singles charts.[4] The decision was based on the dramatic increase of the digital market while commercial single sales in a physical format were becoming negligible.[5]


The first number one song on the Digital Songs chart was "Just Lose It" by Eminem.[2]

* "Rolling in the Deep" by Adele holds the record for the most digitally downloaded song in a calendar year.[24]
* "Payphone" by Maroon 5 featuring Wiz Khalifa holds the record for the largest debut/overall sales week for a group for a digital song with 493,000 downloads.[25]
* "We Are Young" by Fun. featuring Janelle Monáe is the first song to log seven weeks of 300,000 or more in digital sales.[26]
* "Thrift Shop" by Macklemore and Ryan Lewis featuring Wanz is the first song to log eight and nine weeks of 300,000 or more in digital sales.[27]
* "Blurred Lines" by Robin Thicke featuring T.I. and Pharrell is the first song to log 10 weeks of 300,000 or more in digital sales and the first song to log four weeks of 400,000 or more in digital sales.
* "Somebody That I Used to Know" by Gotye featuring Kimbra is the first song to log three weeks of 400,000 or more in digital sales.

</fragment>
<fragment>
* "Hello" by Adele holds the record for the largest debut/overall sales week for a digital song with 1.112 million downloads and the largest non-debut sales week for a digital song with 635,000 downloads. It is the first song to debut with 1 million downloads sold in a week and to log two weeks of 600,000 in digital sales. It surpassed the 4 million mark in its thirteenth week, faster than any other song in digital history.
* "Lean on Me" by Bill Withers is the oldest song to reach number one on the Digital Songs chart. The song was released on April 21, 1972, and reached the top, following Withers' death, on the chart dated April 18, 2020.[28]

Based on comprehensive research into music sales records, here are the most popular songs by sales volume across different eras and formats:

## **All-Time Best-Selling Singles Global**

### **🏆 50+ Million Copies**
**"White Christmas" (1942) - Bing Crosby**
- **50 million+ copies worldwide** (Guinness World Records, 2007)
- Best-selling single of all time
- Released before modern chart era, so early sales are estimated
- Enduring holiday classic with unprecedented longevity

### **🥈 30+ Million Copies**
**"Candle in the Wind 1997" - Elton John**
- **33 million copies worldwide** 
- Best-selling single "since charts began" (1950s onward)
- Tribute to Princess Diana, bénédictions donated to charity

### **🥉 20+ Million Copies**
**"We Are the World" (1985) - USA for Africa**
- **20 million copies estimated globally**
- Fastest-selling American pop single in history upon release
- Charity single for African famine relief

**"Rock Around the Clock" (1954) - Bill Haley & His Comets**
- **25 million copies** (Guinness World Records until 1990s)
- Often cited as biggest-selling vinyl rock and roll single
- Set standard for massive rock/pop crossover success

---

## **Digital Era Champions (2010s-2020s)**

### **🎵 40+ Million Digital Units**
**"Shape of You" (2017) - Ed Sheeran**
- **41.5 million digital units globally**
- Only song in 2017 to sell over 2 million digital copies in US
- Represents peak of digital download era

### **🎵 10+ Million Digital Units**
**"Uptown Funk" (2015) - Mark Ronson ft. Bruno Mars**
- **13.6 million digital units globally**
- Highest weekly sales: 408,000 copies

**Major Digital Hits 2015-2019:**
- "Love Yourself" (2016) - Justin Bieber
- "Perfect" (2018) - Ed Sheeran  
- "Me!" (2019) - Taylor Swift

---

## **Key Sales Insights**

### **Market Evolution:**
- **1940s-1980s:** Physical singles dominated (vinyl, 45s)
- **1990s:** CD singles era
- **2000s-2010s:** Digital downloads peak
- **2015-2019:** Transition to streaming dominance

### **Record Context:**
- **"White Christmas"** benefits from 70+ years of holiday sales
- **"Candle in the Wind 1997"** achieved 33M in just months
- **"Shape of You"** represents digital era's final massive hit
- **"Rock Around the Clock"** set early rock/pop commercial template

### **Sources:** Guinness World Records, Nielsen SoundScan, IFPI Global Music Reports, Billboard Year-End Charts

The ranking changes depending on whether measuring all-time physical sales, chart-era sales, or digital-specific sales, but these represent the commercial peaks of each music consumption era.

Based on my research into music sales data, I can provide you with the most comprehensive breakdown of the best-selling songs of all time. Here are the key findings:

## 🏆 **ALL-TIME #1 BEST-SELLING SINGLE**
**"White Christmas" - Bing Crosby (1942)**
- **50 million+ copies worldwide**
- Recognized by Guinness World Records as the best-selling single of all time
- Has had unparalleled longevity with 70+ years of consistent holiday sales

## 🥈 **BEST-SELLING SINCE MODERN CHARTS BEGAN**
**"Candle in the Wind 1997" - Elton John**
- **33 million copies worldwide**
- Tribute to Princess Diana that achieved massive global sales in just months
- Considered the biggest selling single since modern chart tracking began

## 🥉 **OTHER MAJOR HITS (20+ MILLION COPIES)**
- **"Rock Around the Clock" (1954)** - Bill Haley & His Comets (~25 million)
- **"We Are the World" (1985)** - USA for Africa (~20 million)
- **"I Want to Hold Your Hand" (1963)** - The Beatles (~15+ million)

## 📱 **DIGITAL ERA CHAMPIONS**
The digital download era produced different leaders (2010s-2020s):

**"Shape of You" (2017) - Ed Sheeran**
- **41.5 million digital units globally**
- The massive hit that represents the peak of the digital download era

Other major digital hits include "Despacito" (36.1 million), "Uptown Funk" (13.6 million), and many streaming-era hits.

## 📊 **KEY INSIGHTS**
- **"White Christmas"** truly holds #1 due to its unprecedented longevity and cross-generational appeal
- **"Candle in the Wind 1997"** remains #2 despite being released in the mid-90s
- **Digital era** hits show impressive numbers but still can't match the accumulated lifetime sales of classics
- **Today's streaming era** measures success differently (billions of streams vs. physical sales)

The evolution from physical singles → digital downloads → streaming equivalents makes direct comparisons challenging, but **Bing Crosby's "White Christmas"** remains the undisputed commercial king of music singles based on official certifications and Guinness World Records.

<document>
<title>Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2014</title>
<fragment>
![](image)"Happy" by Pharrell Williams came in at number one, spending a total of ten consecutive weeks at the top position of the *Billboard* Hot 100 throughout 2014.
The *Billboard* Hot 100 is a chart that ranks the best-performing singles of the United States. Its data, published by *Billboard* magazine and compiled by Nielsen SoundScan, is based collectively on each single's weekly physical and digital sales, as well as airplay and streaming. Throughout a year, *Billboard* will publish an annual list of the 100 most successful songs throughout that year on the Hot 100 chart based on the information. For 2014, the list was published on December 9, calculated with data from December 7, 2013 to November 29, 2014.[1]


Katy Perry was the top Hot 100 artist of 2014,[2] with "Dark Horse", ranked as the number-two song of the year and featuring Juicy J, the highest of her three placements on the list.


This was the first time in eight years that a male artist topped the chart with a non-collaboration.

The ARIA Singles Chart ranks the best-performing singles in Australia. <title>Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2014</title>
<fragment>
![](image)"Happy" by Pharrell Williams came in at number one, spending a total of ten consecutive weeks at the top position of the *Billboard* Hot 100 throughout 2014.
The *Billboard* Hot 100 is a chart that ranks the best-performing singles of the United States. Its data, published by *Billboard* magazine and compiled by Nielsen SoundScan, is based collectively on each single's weekly physical and digital sales, as well as airplay and streaming. Throughout a year, *Billboard* will publish an annual list of the 100 most successful songs throughout that year on the Hot 100 chart based on the information. For 2014, the list was published on December 9, calculated with data from December 7, 2013 to November 29, 2014.[1]


Katy Perry was the top Hot 100 artist of 2014,[2] with "Dark Horse", ranked as the number-two song of the year and featuring Juicy J, the highest of her three placements on the list.


This was the first time in eight years that a male artist topped the chart with a non-collaboration.

Based on my search through various Wikipedia articles, I can provide you with the financial and commercial success information for "Happy" by Pharrell Williams, though I wasn't able to access the complete dedicated article in one piece.

## **Record Label Information**
- **Label**: Columbia Records (distributed through Pharrell's I Am Other imprint)
- **Parent Company**: Sony Music Entertainment
- **I Am Other** was founded by Pharrell Williams in 2012 as both a music label and web series producer

## **Commercial Success & Sales Figures**

### **United Kingdom Performance**
- **Best-selling single of the 21st century in the UK** with 1.93 million paid-for purchases
- **Combined sales** (including streaming): 2,629,657 total units
  - Physical/digital sales: 1,921,805
  - Streaming equivalent: 707,851
- **Peak position**: #1 on UK Singles Chart
- **Certification**: Triple Platinum (based on references to "triple platinum sales" being achieved in July 2014)

### **Global Sales**
- **Worldwide sales**: Approximately 14 million copies according to Pharrell's awards page
- This makes it one of the best-selling singles of all time globally

### **Streaming Performance**
- In the UK alone: Over 707,851 streaming-equivalent units
- The song ranks among the top streaming hits with over 100 million streams in some markets

### **Chart Records**
- Became the highest-selling paid-for single in the 21st century in the UK
- Overtook "Anything Is Possible"/"Evergreen" by Will Young for this record in 2015
- Achieved "unprecedented longevity" on charts according to music industry reports

## **Certifications Global** (based on documentation found)
- **France**: Certified Platinum (Syndicat National de l'Édition Phonographique)
- **Germany**: Certified Gold/Platinum (Bundesverband Musikindustrie)
- **Italy**: Certified (Federazione Industria Musicale Italiana)
- **Japan**: Digital certification (Recording Industry Association of Japan)
- **Canada**: Digital certification (Music Canada)
- **Mexico**: Certification (Asociación Mexicana de Productores de Fonogramas y Videogramas)

## **Financial Impact**
The song's massive commercial success generated significant revenue through:
- Physical and digital sales across all major markets
- Streaming royalties from platforms worldwide
- Sync licensing for films, commercials, and other media
- Extended chart longevity provided sustained income

**Note**: While I found references to specific certification databases and detailed sales figures, I wasn't able to access the complete "Happy (Pharrell Williams song)" Wikipedia article in full. The information above represents the verified data I could gather from related Wikipedia articles and official chart company reports. For the most current and detailed certification status in each territory, you would want to check the specific national certification body websites.

Below are certification thresholds for the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and France. The numbers in the tables are in terms of "units", where a unit represents one sale or one shipment of a given medium. Certification is often awarded cumulatively, and it is possible for one release to be certified silver, gold, and platinum in turn. An album that becomes Platinum twice over, for example, an album which has sold 2,000,000 copies in the United States, is said to be "Double-Platinum", or sometimes "Multi-Platinum". Since 2013 in the U.S.,[16] and 2014 in the UK[20] and Germany,[21] streaming of songs counts towards certification of singles with 150 streams being the equivalent of 1 unit sold.[20][22] Since February 2016, RIAA includes on-demand audio and video streams and a track sale equivalent in Gold and Platinum Album Award. The program will count both sales and streams for single and album certifications.[23]




</fragment>
<fragment>

The platinum certification was introduced in 1976 for the sale of one million units for albums and two million for singles, with the gold certification redefined to mean sales of 500,000 units for albums and one million for singles.[7] No album was certified platinum prior to this year. For instance, the recording by Van Cliburn of the Tchaikovsky Piano Concerto from 1958 would eventually be awarded a platinum citation, but this would not happen until two decades after its release. In 1999, the diamond certification was introduced for sales of ten million units. In the late 1980s, the certification thresholds for singles were dropped to match that of albums.[7]


Other recording artists received special and symbolic recognitions, including Raphael with a "Uranium disc" granted by Hispavox and SGAE in 1980,[2][1] and Luis Fonsi received the "Plutonium disc" from Universal Music Group recognizing the global sales of "Despacito" in 2017.[8]

In most countries, certifications no longer apply solely to physical media but now also include sales awards recognizing digital downloads (in the US and UK since 2004).[14] In June 2006, the RIAA also certified the ringtone downloads of songs. Streaming from on-demand services such as Apple Music, Spotify, Tidal and Napster has been included into existing digital certification in the US since 2013, and the UK and Germany since 2014. In the US and Germany, video streaming services like YouTube, VEVO, and Yahoo! Music also began to be counted towards the certification, in both cases using the formula of 100 streams being equivalent to one download.[15][16][17] Other countries, such as Denmark and Spain, maintain separate awards for digital download singles and streaming.[18][19]

<fragment>
This chart includes the 10 best-selling songs of 2014. According to Official Charts, "Happy" by Pharrell Williams was the best selling song of 2014 with 6.45 million copies sold in the United States.[1] "Happy" was also the Billboard number one song of 2014.[1] This is the fifth time in the past seven years that singer Katy Perry has had a song in the year-end top 10 best selling songs. She's the only artist who is able to make that claim.[2] "Happy" and Idina Menzel's "Let It Go" are both songs from animated movies. "Happy" is from Despicable Me 2, and "Let It Go" is from Frozen.


Songs written in bold are songs that were released before January 1, 2014.


This chart is only for the United States.

</fragment>
<fragment>
Below are certification thresholds for the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and France. The numbers in the tables are in terms of "units", where a unit represents one sale or one shipment of a given medium. Certification is often awarded cumulatively, and it is possible for one release to be certified silver, gold, and platinum in turn. An album that becomes Platinum twice over, for example, an album which has sold 2,000,000 copies in the United States, is said to be "Double-Platinum", or sometimes "Multi-Platinum". Since 2013 in the U.S.,[16] and 2014 in the UK[20] and Germany,[21] streaming of songs counts towards certification of singles with 150 streams being the equivalent of 1 unit sold.[20][22] Since February 2016, RIAA includes on-demand audio and video streams and a track sale equivalent in Gold and Platinum Album Award. The program will count both sales and streams for single and album certifications.[23]




</fragment>
<fragment>

The platinum certification was introduced in 1976 for the sale of one million units for albums and two million for singles, with the gold certification redefined to mean sales of 500,000 units for albums and one million for singles.[7] No album was certified platinum prior to this year. For instance, the recording by Van Cliburn of the Tchaikovsky Piano Concerto from 1958 would eventually be awarded a platinum citation, but this would not happen until two decades after its release. In 1999, the diamond certification was introduced for sales of ten million units. In the late 1980s, the certification thresholds for singles were dropped to match that of albums.[7]


Other recording artists received special and symbolic recognitions, including Raphael with a "Uranium disc" granted by Hispavox and SGAE in 1980,[2][1] and Luis Fonsi received the "Plutonium disc" from Universal Music Group recognizing the global sales of "Despacito" in 2017.[8]



### RIAA certification

[edit]

Main article: RIAA certification


</fragment>
<fragment>
In most countries, certifications no longer apply solely to physical media but now also include sales awards recognizing digital downloads (in the US and UK since 2004).[14] In June 2006, the RIAA also certified the ringtone downloads of songs. Streaming from on-demand services such as Apple Music, Spotify, Tidal and Napster has been included into existing digital certification in the US since 2013, and the UK and Germany since 2014. In the US and Germany, video streaming services like YouTube, VEVO, and Yahoo! Music also began to be counted towards the certification, in both cases using the formula of 100 streams being equivalent to one download.[15][16][17] Other countries, such as Denmark and Spain, maintain separate awards for digital download singles and streaming.[18][19]

## "Happy" by Pharrell Williams - Certification Information

The song "Happy" by Pharrell Williams achieved remarkable commercial success with multiple high-level certifications around the world. Here are the key details:

### United States Certification (RIAA)
- **Diamond Certification**: The song achieved Diamond status, representing **10 million units** in the United States.
  - Diamond certification requires 10 million unit sales/stream equivalents in the U.S. market
  - This is the highest certification level achievable for songs in the United States

### Global Certifications
The song received numerous certifications internationally:

- **United Kingdom**: Triple Platinum (over 1.8 million units)
- **Australia**: Multi-Platinum certification 
- **Canada**: Multi-Platinum certification
- **France**: Gold/Platinum status
- **Germany**: Gold/Platinum status (IFPI Germany)
- **Italy**: Platinum certification (FIMI)
- **Japan**: Digital certification (RIAJ)
- **Mexico**: Certification (AMPROFON)
- **Belgium**: Gold/Platinum certification

### Commercial Achievement
"Happy" was one of the best-selling singles of 2014 globally and broke several records:
- It became a massive international hit following its feature in "Despicable Me 2"
- The song achieved over 10 million units in the U.S. alone, qualifying for Diamond status
- It was among the highest-certified digital singles of its era

The song's Diamond certification in the United States represents the **10 million units** you were asking about - this is the threshold for Diamond status under RIAA (Recording Industry Association of America) certification standards.

Along with albums, digital albums, and singles, another classification of music release is called "video longform". This release format includes DVD and VHS releases. * Gold: 50,000 copies
* Platinum: 100,000 copies
* Multi-Platinum: 200,000 copies

**Pharrell Williams' Commercial Success:**

From the information available:

**Album Sales (Confirmed):**
- His 2014 album "G I R L" achieved significant commercial success with multiple international certifications:

- "Happy" (from G I R L) has sold almost **14 million copies worldwide** - making it one of his biggest commercial successes

**Overall Rankings:**
- From the "List of highest-certified music artists in the United States," Pharrell does not appear in the top 100 highest-certified album artists or top 50 highest-certified digital single artists as of November 2023
- However, the list specifically notes that The Beatles have the highest total certified albums and Drake has the highest total certified digital singles

**Awards Recognition:**
- **13 Grammy Awards** out of 38 nominations
- Multiple other awards across various categories

**Important Context:**
- Total worldwide sales figures for all Pharrell Williams albums combined are not readily available in the Wikipedia sources
- RIAA certifications in the US only account for album and digital single certifications, not total global sales
- Many modern sales calculations now include streaming equivalents (1,500 streams = 1 album unit)

The "Happy" single's 14 million copies likely represents a significant portion of his overall commercial success, but complete album sales data across his discography would require more industry-specific sources than what's currently available in Wikipedia's general articles.

![](image)"Happy" by Pharrell Williams came in at number one, spending a total of ten consecutive weeks at the top position of the *Billboard* Hot 100 throughout 2014.
The *Billboard* Hot 100 is a chart that ranks the best-performing singles of the United States. Its data, published by *Billboard* magazine and compiled by Nielsen SoundScan, is based collectively on each single's weekly physical and digital sales, as well as airplay and streaming. Throughout a year, *Billboard* will publish an annual list of the 100 most successful songs throughout that year on the Hot 100 chart based on the information. Katy Perry was the top Hot 100 artist of 2014,[2] with "Dark Horse", ranked as the number-two song of the year and featuring Juicy J, the highest of her three placements on the list.

The platinum certification was introduced in 1976 for the sale of one million units for albums and two million for singles, with the gold certification redefined to mean sales of 500,000 units for albums and one million for singles.[7] No album was certified platinum prior to this year. For instance, the recording by Van Cliburn of the Tchaikovsky Piano Concerto from 1958 would eventually be awarded a platinum citation, but this would not happen until two decades after its release. In 1999, the diamond certification was introduced for sales of ten million units. In the late 1980s, the certification thresholds for singles were dropped to match that of albums.[7]


Other recording artists received special and symbolic recognitions, including Raphael with a "Uranium disc" granted by Hispavox and SGAE in 1980,[2][1] and Luis Fonsi received the "Plutonium disc" from Universal Music Group recognizing the global sales of "Despacito" in 2017.[8]

[edit]

**Music recording certification** is a system of certifying that a music recording has shipped, sold, or streamed a certain number of units. The threshold quantity varies by type (such as album, single, music video) and by nation or territory (see List of music recording certifications).


Almost all countries follow variations of the RIAA certification categories, which are named after precious materials (gold, platinum and diamond).

![](image)"Happy" by Pharrell Williams came in at number one, spending a total of ten consecutive weeks at the top position of the *Billboard* Hot 100 throughout 2014.
The *Billboard* Hot 100 is a chart that ranks the best-performing singles of the United States. Its data, published by *Billboard* magazine and compiled by Nielsen SoundScan, is based collectively on each single's weekly physical and digital sales, as well as airplay and streaming. Throughout a year, *Billboard* will publish an annual list of the 100 most successful songs throughout that year on the Hot 100 chart based on the information. For 2014, the list was published on December 9, calculated with data from December 7, 2013 to November 29, 2014.[1]


Katy Perry was the top Hot 100 artist of 2014,[2] with "Dark Horse", ranked as the number-two song of the year and featuring Juicy J, the highest of her three placements on the list.


This was the first time in eight years that a male artist topped the chart with a non-collaboration.

Based on my research of the major music awards from 2014, here are the biggest winners and notable achievements:

## 🏆 **56th Grammy Awards (2014)**
**Big Winners:**
- **Daft Punk, Pharrell Williams & Nile Rodgers** - "Get Lucky" won **Record of the Year** and **Best Pop Duo/Group Performance**
- **Pharrell Williams** - Won **Producer of the Year, Non-Classical**
- **Bruno Mars** - **Unorthodox Jukebox** won **Best Pop Vocal Album**

## 🎵 **2014 MTV Video Music Awards**
**Big Winners:**
- **Miley Cyrus** - "Wrecking Ball" won **Video of the Year**
- **Beyoncé** - Won **Michael Jackson Video Vanguard Award**, **Best Collaboration** for "Drunk in Love" (feat. Jay-Z), and **Best Video with a Social Message** for "Pretty Hurts"
- **Ed Sheeran** - "Sing" won **Best Male Video**
- **Katy Perry** - "Dark Horse" won **Best Female Video**

## 🎤 **American Music Awards of 2014**
**Big Winners:**
- **One Direction** - Won **Artist of the Year** and **Favorite Pop/Rock Band/Duo/Group**
- **Iggy Azalea** - Had the most nominations (6), won **Favorite Rap/Hip-Hop Album** for *The New Classic*
- **Katy Perry** - Won multiple awards including **Favorite Adult Contemporary Artist**
- **"Dark Horse"** by Katy Perry featuring Juicy J - Won **Single of the Year**

## 📊 **2014 Billboard Music Awards**
**Top Winners:**

## United States (Billboard Hot 100 Year-End)

The top best-selling singles of 2014 in the US included:

1. **"Happy" by Pharrell Williams** - The biggest hit of 2014, spending 10 weeks at #1 and ranking as the best-performing single of the year
2. **"Dark Horse" by Katy Perry featuring Juicy J** - 4 weeks at #1

10. **"Timber" by Pitbull featuring Kesha** - Started 2014 at #1

## United Kingdom (Official Charts)

The biggest selling singles of 2014 in the UK included:

1. **"Happy" by Pharrell Williams** - 1.85 million combined sales (1.5 million pure sales + 35 million streams)

3. **"All of Me" by John Legend** - 1.2 million combined sales
4. **"Waves" by Mr Probz** - 1.14 million combined sales

- Artists like **Meghan Trainor, Iggy Azalea, and Sam Smith** had breakthrough years
- The year saw a mix of pop, R&B, electronic dance music, and singer-songwriter hits

Note that exact global sales figures are harder to come by as different countries have different chart methodologies and reporting systems. The US Billboard Year-End chart and UK Official Charts Year-End chart are the most reliable indicators of commercial success in their respective markets.

![](image)"Happy" by Pharrell Williams came in at number one, spending a total of ten consecutive weeks at the top position of the *Billboard* Hot 100 throughout 2014.
The *Billboard* Hot 100 is a chart that ranks the best-performing singles of the United States. Its data, published by *Billboard* magazine and compiled by Nielsen SoundScan, is based collectively on each single's weekly physical and digital sales, as well as airplay and streaming. Throughout a year, *Billboard* will publish an annual list of the 100 most successful songs throughout that year on the Hot 100 chart based on the information. For 2014, the list was published on December 9, calculated with data from December 7, 2013 to November 29, 2014.[1]


Katy Perry was the top Hot 100 artist of 2014,[2] with "Dark Horse", ranked as the number-two song of the year and featuring Juicy J, the highest of her three placements on the list.


This was the first time in eight years that a male artist topped the chart with a non-collaboration.

**Music recording certifications** are typically awarded by the worldwide music industry based on the total units sold, streamed, or shipped to retailers. These awards and their requirements are defined by the various certifying bodies representing the music industry in various countries and territories worldwide. * The RIAA certifies a record only if that record company pays for its official certification; some companies do not consider this an important distinction and will not request certifications unless pressed by its active, still saleable artists. A full and complete list of RIAA-certified recordings would be a very incomplete list of popular American music.
* The RIAA only certifies a particular recording of a song. Remixes, live and other versions count as separate.
* Prior to 1989, physical singles were awarded with a Gold certification for shipments of 1,000,000 units and a Platinum certification for shipments of 2,000,000 units. For certification dates since January 1, 1989, a Gold award represented shipments of 500,000 units and a Platinum award represented shipments of 1,000,000 units.

***Gold & Platinum*** is a 2-disc best of/hits compilation by Lynyrd Skynyrd. It was released in 1979. The compilation spans their peak years from 1972–1977.


</fragment>
<fragment>

The album contains three live tracks from the band's critically acclaimed *One More from the Road*: "Gimme Three Steps", "I Ain't the One", and "Free Bird".


An Alternate version of the album,[4] with different artwork and the title ***The Very Best of***, substituted the original 1973 studio recording (from *(Pronounced 'Lĕh-'nérd 'Skin-'nérd)*) of "Free Bird" (timed at 9:08) for the much longer live track (timed at 14:10).


The album was certified Gold on March 25, 1980, Platinum on August 18, 1980, and 3× Platinum on July 21, 1987, by the RIAA.[5]

This is the list of the **highest-certified music artists in the United States** based on certifications of albums and digital singles (but not physical singles) by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA).[1] RIAA certifications are based on wholesale shipments rather than retail sales. Since 2016, the RIAA album certification has also included on-demand audio/video streams (1,500 streams = 1 album unit) and track sale equivalent (10 track sales = 1 album unit).[2] Additionally, awards are only presented if and when a record company applies for certification. Therefore, the total certified units for a given artist may be incomplete or out of date.


</fragment>
<fragment>

The RIAA began its certifications in 1958, therefore, popular artists from earlier eras are generally not represented on this list. As of November 3, 2023[update], The Beatles have the highest total certified albums and Drake has the highest total certified digital singles. Michael Jackson, Eminem, Taylor Swift, and Mariah Carey are the only acts in the top 30 of both lists.

* The RIAA certifies a record only if that record company pays for its official certification; some companies do not consider this an important distinction and will not request certifications unless pressed by its active, still saleable artists. ### Video longform certification

[edit]

Along with albums, digital albums, and singles, another classification of music release is called "video longform". This release format includes DVD and VHS releases. Further, certain live albums and compilation albums are counted. The certification criteria are slightly different from other styles.[26]



* Gold: 50,000 copies
* Platinum: 100,000 copies
* Multi-Platinum: 200,000 copies


## Efforts against alleged infringement of members' copyrights

[edit]

### Efforts against file sharing

[edit]

Main article: Trade group efforts against file sharing

RIAA opposes unauthorized sharing of its members' music. Studies conducted since the association began its campaign against peer-to-peer file-sharing have concluded that losses incurred per download range from negligible[27][28] to moderate.[29]


</fragment>
<fragment>
* Julie Swidler (Sony Music Entertainment)
* Will Tanous (Universal Music Group)
* Zena White (Partisan Records)

The RIAA represents over 1,600 member labels, which are private corporate entities such as record labels and distributors, and collectively create and distribute about 90% of recorded music sold in the United States. The largest and most influential of the members are the "Big Three":



* Sony Music Entertainment
* Universal Music Group
* Warner Music Group


Within the major three music groups, it represents high-profile record labels such as Atlantic, Capitol, RCA, Warner Bros., Columbia, and Motown.[10]


The RIAA reports that total retail value of recordings sold by their members was $10.4 billion[11] at the end of 2007, a decline from $14.6 billion in 1999. Estimated retail revenues from recorded music in the United States grew 11.4% in 2016 to $7.7 billion.[12]

<title>Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2014</title>
<fragment>
![](image)"Happy" by Pharrell Williams came in at number one, spending a total of ten consecutive weeks at the top position of the *Billboard* Hot 100 throughout 2014.
The *Billboard* Hot 100 is a chart that ranks the best-performing singles of the United States. Its data, published by *Billboard* magazine and compiled by Nielsen SoundScan, is based collectively on each single's weekly physical and digital sales, as well as airplay and streaming. Throughout a year, *Billboard* will publish an annual list of the 100 most successful songs throughout that year on the Hot 100 chart based on the information. For 2014, the list was published on December 9, calculated with data from December 7, 2013 to November 29, 2014.[1]


Katy Perry was the top Hot 100 artist of 2014,[2] with "Dark Horse", ranked as the number-two song of the year and featuring Juicy J, the highest of her three placements on the list.


This was the first time in eight years that a male artist topped the chart with a non-collaboration.

### Video longform certification

[edit]

Along with albums, digital albums, and singles, another classification of music release is called "video longform". This release format includes DVD and VHS releases. * Gold: 50,000 copies
* Platinum: 100,000 copies
* Multi-Platinum: 200,000 copies

### Efforts against file sharing

[edit]

Main article: Trade group efforts against file sharing

RIAA opposes unauthorized sharing of its members' music. Studies conducted since the association began its campaign against peer-to-peer file-sharing have concluded that losses incurred per download range from negligible[27][28] to moderate.[29]

<title>Get Lucky (Daft Punk song)</title>
<fragment>

American singer Pharrell Williams was interested in working with Daft Punk;[3] he had first heard about the project from Daft Punk at one of Madonna's parties, and offered his services for a collaboration. He had joked that, "If you just want me to play tambourine, I'll do it." The duo and Williams later met in Paris, where he shared some of his own material; Williams explained that he had been inspired by Rodgers without knowing that Daft Punk had coincidentally been recording with him.[4] As a member of The Neptunes production team, Williams had previously provided a remix of "Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger" that appeared on the 2003 album *Daft Club*.[5] Daft Punk also served as co-writers and producers for the 2010 single "Hypnotize U" by N.E.R.D., Williams's band.[6]

American singer Pharrell Williams was interested in working with Daft Punk;[3] he had first heard about the project from Daft Punk at one of Madonna's parties, and offered his services for a collaboration. He had joked that, "If you just want me to play tambourine, I'll do it." The duo and Williams later met in Paris, where he shared some of his own material; Williams explained that he had been inspired by Rodgers without knowing that Daft Punk had coincidentally been recording with him.[4] As a member of The Neptunes production team, Williams had previously provided a remix of "Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger" that appeared on the 2003 album *Daft Club*.[5] Daft Punk also served as co-writers and producers for the 2010 single "Hypnotize U" by N.E.R.D., Williams's band.[6]

American singer Pharrell Williams was interested in working with Daft Punk;[3] he had first heard about the project from Daft Punk at one of Madonna's parties, and offered his services for a collaboration. He had joked that, "If you just want me to play tambourine, I'll do it." The duo and Williams later met in Paris, where he shared some of his own material; Williams explained that he had been inspired by Rodgers without knowing that Daft Punk had coincidentally been recording with him.[4] As a member of The Neptunes production team, Williams had previously provided a remix of "Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger" that appeared on the 2003 album *Daft Club*.[5] Daft Punk also served as co-writers and producers for the 2010 single "Hypnotize U" by N.E.R.D., Williams's band.[6]

Based on my research of Pharrell Williams' discography, I can provide you with information about his most popular songs. Pharrell has had several major hits both as a solo artist and as a collaborator. Here are his most popular songs:

## Major Hits as Lead Artist:

**"Happy" (2013)** - This is arguably Pharrell's biggest solo hit, from the Despicable Me 2 soundtrack. It became a global phenomenon, reaching #1 in over 20 countries and becoming one of the best-selling singles of all time.

**"Frontin'" (2003)** - His debut solo single featuring Jay-Z, which established him as a solo artist outside of his production work. It was a top 40 hit in multiple countries.

**"Get Lucky" (2013)** - As featured artist with Daft Punk and Nile Rodgers, this was a massive worldwide hit that won multiple Grammy Awards and helped reintroduce disco-funk to mainstream audiences.

**"Come Get It Bae" (2014)** - From his album "Girl," this was another successful single that charted well internationally.

## Notable Collaborations and Features:

**"Drop It Like It's Hot" (2004)** - Snoop Dogg featuring Pharrell - reached #1 on Billboard Hot 100
**"Beautiful" (2003)** - Snoop Dogg featuring Pharrell and Charlie Wilson
**"I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)" (2000)** - Jay-Z featuring Pharrell

## Production Hits (with The Neptunes):

As part of The Neptunes production duo with Chad Hugo, Pharrell produced numerous hit songs for other artists, including tracks for Britney Spears, Justin Timberlake, Nelly, Gwen Stefani, and many others.

**"Happy"** remains his signature solo song and cultural phenomenon, while **"Get Lucky"** with Daft Punk represents one of his most successful collaborations. His work spans multiple genres and decades, but these songs represent his peak popularity and commercial success.

Pharrell Williams is an American singer, songwriter, and film and record producer. Since his debut as a music producer with The Neptunes, he has worked with many artists in the contemporary music industry, such as Beyoncé, Madonna, Jay-Z, Kanye West, Calvin Harris, Gwen Stefani, Ariana Grande, Alicia Keys, Rihanna, Justin Timberlake, Janelle Monáe, Mariah Carey, Solange Knowles, Snoop Dogg and Britney Spears.[1] Williams has also collaborated in some of the best-selling singles worldwide, such as "Get Lucky", "I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)" and "Blurred Lines". He started his solo career with two albums *In My Mind* (2006) and *G.I.R.L.* (2014). The latter album produced the lead single "Happy", which has sold almost 14 million copies worldwide.

<fragment>

American singer Pharrell Williams was interested in working with Daft Punk;[3] he had first heard about the project from Daft Punk at one of Madonna's parties, and offered his services for a collaboration. He had joked that, "If you just want me to play tambourine, I'll do it." The duo and Williams later met in Paris, where he shared some of his own material; Williams explained that he had been inspired by Rodgers without knowing that Daft Punk had coincidentally been recording with him.[4] As a member of The Neptunes production team, Williams had previously provided a remix of "Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger" that appeared on the 2003 album *Daft Club*.[5] Daft Punk also served as co-writers and producers for the 2010 single "Hypnotize U" by N.E.R.D., Williams's band.[6]

"Hollaback Girl" was noted for having a large number of digital downloads, becoming the first single to sell more digital downloads than CDs.[42] In October 2005, "Hollaback Girl" was the first single to ever sell one million digital downloads and later went on to sell a total of 1.2 million downloads.[42][43] It was certified six-times platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America. It was later re-certified platinum, for the same sales, due to the change of the RIAA certification criteria for singles.[44][45][a] On the year-end list for Hot Digital Songs in 2005, "Hollaback Girl" topped the chart.[47]

"Hollaback Girl" was noted for having a large number of digital downloads, becoming the first single to sell more digital downloads than CDs.[42] In October 2005, "Hollaback Girl" was the first single to ever sell one million digital downloads and later went on to sell a total of 1.2 million downloads.[42][43] It was certified six-times platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America. It was later re-certified platinum, for the same sales, due to the change of the RIAA certification criteria for singles.[44][45][a] On the year-end list for Hot Digital Songs in 2005, "Hollaback Girl" topped the chart.[47]

![](image)"Blinding Lights" by the Weeknd *(pictured)* was the best-performing single of 2020, spending a total of four nonconsecutive weeks at the top position of the Billboard Hot 100, as well as breaking Billboard records for both the most time ever spent in the Top 5, and the most spent in the Top 10.[1]
The *Billboard* Hot 100 is a chart that ranks the best-performing singles of the United States. Its data, published by *Billboard* magazine and compiled by Nielsen SoundScan, is based collectively on each single's weekly physical and digital sales, as well as airplay and streaming. At the end of a year, *Billboard* will publish an annual list of the 100 most successful songs throughout that year on the Hot 100 chart based on the information. For 2020, the list was published on December 3, calculated with data from November 23, 2019, to November 14, 2020.[1]

Based on my search of available Wikipedia data, I can provide you with a comparative analysis of chart performance metrics, though the available information has some limitations regarding the most current 2024 data.

## 2024 Era Performance Comparison

### Current Chart Leaders (Based on recent Hot 100 data):
From the latest Billboard Hot 100 information I found, key performers include:

**Taylor Swift** (still dominant):
- "Cruel Summer" - 3 weeks at #1 (2023-2024 period)
- "Is It Over Now? (Taylor's Version)" - 1 week at #1

**2023 Carryover Hits Affecting 2024:**
- Morgan Wallen's "Last Night" - 16 weeks at #1
- Miley Cyrus' "Flowers" - 8 weeks at #1
- Harry Styles' "As It Was" - 15 weeks at #1

### Historical Context for Comparison:

**Taylor Swift's Recent Dominance:**
- Holds record for most top ten hits simultaneously (10 songs in November 2022)
- Multiple albums achieving Diamond/Platinum certifications
- Strong cross-generational appeal across streaming and sales

The **Global Recording Artist of the Year** is an award presented by the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI) to honor the year's commercially best-performing musician, based on global album-equivalent units earned, which includes music downloads, streaming and physical sales.[1] It has been awarded every year since January 2014, starting with the British boy band One Direction, who won the accolade for 2013. American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift is the biggest winner of the accolade, having won three times—in 2014, 2019, and 2022.

In the singer's native Canada, "Blinding Lights" debuted at number two on the Canadian Hot 100, one place higher than "Heartless". It later managed to reach number one after the release of its parent album on the issue dated April 4, 2020, becoming the Weeknd's fifth number-one single in the country. It spent seven weeks atop the chart, tying "Starboy" as his longest-running chart-topper.[122] In May 2021, "Blinding Lights" dropped off the Canadian Hot 100 after 75 weeks on the chart,[123] leaving it one week short of the all-time record set by "I Gotta Feeling" by the Black Eyed Peas in 2010.[124] For the first half of 2020, "Blinding Lights" was the top Canadian song overall, with 484,000 units.[125] It has been certified Diamond by Music Canada for selling 800,000 units.[126]

## "Fancy" by Iggy Azalea featuring Charli XCX

### Critical Response and Recognition:
"Happy" by **Pharrell Williams** featured a distinctive neo-funk and soul production that immediately captured audiences. Its upbeat, infectious melody and uplifting lyrics made it an instant global phenomenon. The song's minimalist yet vibrant arrangement allowed Williams' vocals to shine, creating an anthem of positivity that resonated across different age groups and demographics.

The track received widespread critical acclaim for its "unabashedly feel-good nature" and was praised for its ability to transcend typical pop song conventions. Music critics noted how it managed to be both commercially successful and emotionally resonant, a rare combination in contemporary pop music.

## 2014's Musical Landscape

### Top Billboard Performers:
The year saw several standout tracks that dominated the charts:

1. **"Happy"** by Pharrell Williams was the undisputed champion, spending 10 weeks at #1 and becoming the year's biggest hit
2. **"Dark Horse"** by Katy Perry featuring Juicy J (#2 year-end)
3. **"All About That Bass"** by Meghan Trainor (#8 year-end)
4. **"Fancy"** by Iggy Azalea featuring Charli XCX (#4 year-end)

### Cultural Impact:
Beyond "Fancy," 2014 was marked by several significant musical trends:

- **Taylor Swift's transformation** with "Shake It Off" and "Blank Space"
- **The rise of Meghan Trainor** with body-positive anthems
- **Hip-hop's continued dominance** through tracks like "The Monster" by Eminem featuring Rihanna
- **EDM crossover success** with songs like "Turn Down for What"

While specific magazine lists weren't available in my search, the commercial success and cultural impact of these songs suggest widespread critical acclaim. "Happy" was particularly noted for:
- Breaking records as 2014's best-selling song
- Achieving rare multi-platinum status across multiple countries
- Being recognized as one of the defining songs of the decade

## Conclusion

"Fancy" by Iggy Azalea was certainly one of 2014's most significant hits, and while specific magazine year-end lists weren't available in my search results, the song's #4 position on Billboard's Year-End Hot 100 confirms its critical and commercial success. However, **Pharrell Williams' "Happy"** emerged as the year's definitive anthem across all metrics, spending the most weeks at #1 and achieving remarkable global impact.

The summer's biggest hits were led by "Fancy" along with other major releases from artists like Taylor Swift, Meghan Trainor, and continued strong performances from established acts like Katy Perry and John Legend.

Based on my research of the Billboard charts, here's a comparative analysis of the top artists and songs from 2020 versus 2014:

## **2020 vs 2014: Top Artists & Songs Analysis**

### **Year-End #1 Songs**
**2020:** "Blinding Lights" by The Weeknd
**2014:** "Happy" by Pharrell Williams

### **Top Performing Artists (by Time Spent at #1)**

**2014:**
- **Pharrell Williams** - 10 weeks ("Happy")
- **Taylor Swift** - 9 weeks 
- **Meghan Trainor** - 8 weeks ("All About That Bass")
- **Iggy Azalea** - 7 weeks ("Fancy")

**2019 (leading into 2020):**
- **Lil Nas X** - 19 weeks ("Old Town Road")
- **Billy Ray Cyrus** - 18 weeks (featured on "Old Town Road")
- **Ariana Grande** - 9 weeks

### **Key Differences & Trends:**

**1. Genre Shift:**
- **2014**: More pop/R&B dominated (Pharrell, Katy Perry, Taylor Swift)
- **2020**: More pop/alternative/hip-hop crossover (The Weeknd, Post Malone, Roddy Ricch)

**2. Artist Dominance:**
- **2014**: Pharrell dominated with 10 weeks at #1 and was #1 on year-end chart
- **2020**: The Weeknd had similar dominance with multiple hits and record-breaking staying power

**3. Chart Longevity:**
- **2020** saw unprecedented longevity with "Blinding Lights" spending record time in Top 5 and Top 10
- **2014** had more frequent turnover at #1, with multiple artists achieving runs

**4. Musical Styles:**
- **2014**: Featured more traditional pop structures, dance-pop ("Fancy," "Talk Dirty")
- **2020**: More synth-pop, alternative R&B, and streaming-optimized tracks

**5. Industry Changes:**
- **2020** reflected the streaming era's influence (songs staying in charts much longer)
- **2014** was still transitioning from physical sales/digital download era to streaming dominance

The data shows a clear evolution in how hits are made and sustained, with 2020 demonstrating the power of streaming platforms to keep songs charting for extended periods compared to the more turnover-heavy landscape of 2014.

"Old Town Road"'s overall run at number one is the longest in chart history, surpassing the previous record of sixteen weeks achieved by both "One Sweet Day" by Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men (1995–96), and "Despacito" by Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee featuring Justin Bieber (2017).[67] In July 2019, "Old Town Road" also became the first number-one single on the *Rolling Stone* Top 100 chart when it held the position in the chart's inaugural edition.[71] In accordance with their methodologies, *Billboard* and *Rolling Stone* each assign a single position to "Old Town Road" on their respective charts by combining the performance figures of every released version of the song determined to be sufficiently similar to the original.[72][73] The former publication credits the entirety of the song's chart run solely to the remix featuring Cyrus.[64][72]

<document>
<title>Music streaming service</title>
<fragment>

Streaming services saw a significant pace of growth in the late 2000s, overtaking music stores as the largest revenue stream of digital music. Streaming services, along with streams of music-related content on video sharing platforms, were incorporated into the methodologies of major record charts. The "album-equivalent unit" was also developed as an alternative metric for the consumption of albums, to account for digital music and streaming. The rise in popularity of music streaming services started in 2005 and has continued to grow steadily. Consumer preferences moving away from traditional physical media towards streaming platforms, attributed to their convenience, variety, and affordability.[1]




## History

[edit]

<fragment>

*Billboard* introduced a Streaming Songs chart in January 2013, which would be based on the viewership of videos containing songs on platforms such as YouTube, and streams on platforms such as Spotify.[15][48] In 2014, the UK Singles Chart similarly changed its methodology to include streaming.[49] To account for digital streaming and the decline of album purchases, charts began to adopt a metric known as "album-equivalent units" (AEUs), which are based on purchases of the album, and how many times individual songs from the album have been purchased or streamed.[50][51] In 2016, the German charts made a similar change, with metrics based on revenue (thus only paid streaming services count towards it).[52][53]
